name: JOYCE, the Hon. Barnaby Thomas Gerard

headline.note: Joyce's private farm, accounting, banking and self-employment sequence is documented only at year precision without hours, leave or complete employer names. Army Reserve service does not establish a public full-time interval. Study, party activity and elected office are excluded; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Joyce's website gives study from 1986 to 1989; sources vary between Bachelor of Accounting, Financial Accounting and Bachelor of Financial Administration wording. Study load and employment overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Unidentified farms in northern NSW and Queensland
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract supplies the role and years; biographical accounts place farm work around northern NSW and Queensland and also mention nightclub work without dates. Employers, exact dates, hours, remuneration, leave and continuity are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private farm employment is supported, but no substantive full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Chartered accountancy firm and an American multinational (names unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract gives accountant from 1991 to 1994. Joyce's website says three years at a chartered firm followed by a short American-multinational cost-accounting role, but does not name either employer or identify the transition. Exact dates, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but employer boundaries and full-time status are not established.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen record supplies role and years; Joyce's website describes five years with a major regional bank, creating a boundary discrepancy with the official four-year outer range. Employer, government control, exact dates, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Bank employment is supported, but employer control, exact interval and full-time status are not established.

career_spells.employer: Barnaby Joyce & Co., St George, Queensland
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract gives self-employed accountant from 1998 to 2005. Narrative sources identify the firm and location but variously say it began in 1999 or operated for ten years. Legal registration, exact start/end, hours, leave, staff and whether work continued after Senate commencement are unresolved; the frozen range is retained.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is supported, but conflicting boundaries and unknown hours prevent calculation.

career_spells.employer: Australian Army Reserve — Royal Queensland Regiment
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary material, citing biographical sources, records Army Reserve service from 1996 to 2001. Paid-duty days, hours, rank, breaks and overlap with banking and accountancy work are unresolved; Reserve service is not assumed full-time.
career_spells.counting_note: Public military service is supported, but no substantive full-time interval or FTE is established.

career_spells.employer: National Party of Australia / Liberal National Party of Queensland
career_spells.role: Member, candidate, parliamentary representative and leader
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary material records Nationals membership from 1995, Queensland LNP affiliation during Senate service, and resignation from the Nationals on 27 November 2025. Separate party remuneration and hours are unresolved; parliamentary offices are recorded within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster gives first federal service; secondary parliamentary chronology gives Senate service from 1 July 2005 until resignation on 8 August 2013.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Parliamentary chronology records House service from the 7 September 2013 election until the High Court held the 2016 election invalid on 27 October 2017. Ministerial and party-room offices are nested within this spell.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Joyce returned at the 2 December 2017 by-election and remains the frozen-roster Member for New England. Ministerial, shadow and party-room offices are nested within elected service. No employment is inferred for the parliamentary gap.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster identifies One Nation; secondary material records formal joining on 8 December 2025 after a short independent interval. Remuneration and hours are unresolved and parliamentary service is recorded separately.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook.

sources.note: Secondary synthesis supplies Army Reserve, party and exact parliamentary dates with parliamentary, court, media and biographical citations.

research_notes: The frozen official 1998–2005 self-employment range is retained despite narrative claims that Barnaby Joyce & Co. began in 1999 and operated for ten years.
Unnamed early employers remain unresolved rather than being guessed from industry descriptions.
Army Reserve service overlapped private employment and is not treated as full-time public employment.
House service is split around the 2017 High Court disqualification and by-election; no work is invented for the gap.
open_questions: Which farms employed Joyce from 1989 to 1991, and what were the dates, hours and breaks, including any nightclub work?
What were the names, exact dates, hours and leave for the chartered accountancy firm and American multinational roles?
Which regional bank employed Joyce, under what government control, and on what exact dates and hours?
What were Barnaby Joyce & Co.'s registration, operating dates, staff, hours, leave and any continuation after July 2005?
What paid-duty days, rank, hours and breaks applied to Army Reserve service?
Was there paid non-parliamentary work during the 27 October–2 December 2017 eligibility gap?
